rules: RPE 6 / 7 / 8: finish with approximately 4 / 3 / 2 good repetitions remaining. RPE 3–5 means easy practice, well away from failure.
Weeks 1–2: cap strength exercises at two sets and RPE 6. Keep any lower intensity prescribed below. Use the non-jumping versions described later.
Weeks 3–5: use the tables if soreness and court performance remain manageable. Week 6: halve working sets, rounding up, and cap strength work at RPE 6.
Sets are working sets; warm-ups are additional. Repetitions are per side when stated. For unilateral exercises, allow about 15–30 seconds to switch sides, then take the listed rest after both sides.
Your 80 kg deadlift does not establish your 1RM or your Romanian-deadlift load. Select weights using controlled technique and the prescribed RPE.
progression: Introduce impact gradually. During weeks 1–2, replace Monday’s jump with a quick squat-to-calf raise, without leaving the floor. Thursday stays a lateral step-and-stick. From week 3, introduce low bilateral jumps if walking, stairs and landing practice are comfortable. Introduce small lateral bounds only after bilateral landings are consistently controlled and symptom-free during and the following day. Keep the same exercise slot, sets and reps.

Treat power repetitions separately from lifting RPE. For throws and jumps, RPE describes overall effort—not repetitions remaining before failure. Reset fully; stop when speed, balance or landing quality deteriorates. Do not add weighted jumps or depth jumps during this block.

Progress repetitions before weight. When every set reaches the top of its range at the target RPE on two exposures, add the smallest available load. Have a gym coach check your squat, hinge and landing technique early in the block.
Match unilateral work. Start with the less coordinated side and match its clean repetitions on the other side. Do not automatically add extra sets to the nondominant side.

Respond to court fatigue. If Saturday leaves you moving differently or sore on stairs, keep Sunday comfortable and replace Monday’s jumps with the non-jumping version. Reduce Monday’s lower-body sets by roughly one-third. If Thursday repeatedly makes Saturday footwork sluggish, reduce Thursday’s lower-body exercises to one set until that resolves.

Respond to pain. Stop an exercise that causes sharp or increasing joint/tendon pain. Persistent pain, swelling or altered walking warrants assessment; completing eight exercises does not take priority over that.
